data.why: The app is a pure client-side genome browser with no file-upload workflow of its own other than URL/session loading; its built-in example sessions and track registries under resources/ already give a browser agent real loci, tracks and variant data to open via the Session and Track menus.

goals: Open a reference genome (e.g. hg38) and navigate to a specific locus or gene by name
Load an annotation or alignment track (BAM/CRAM, VCF, bigWig) from the built-in track registry or a URL
Inspect read coverage and alignments across a region, zooming and panning to resolve individual variants
Load a pre-built example session (e.g. the 1000 Genomes variants session or the SKBR3 breast cancer cell line VCF/BAM session) and review the displayed tracks
Save or share the current browser state as a session URL for later reuse
Switch genomes and confirm tracks/session reload correctly, including recovery after a failed genome load

review.summary: The tree states IGV-Web's purpose accurately: pick a reference, add read, variant and annotation layers, inspect a site down to individual reads, then save or share the view. Most nodes are well evidenced and replayed. It needs fixes before filing: the example-session phase holds one failed task and two unconfirmed ones, one cited screen does not show the claimed sort, and core steps are missing (loading your own files, sorting reads at a variant, viewing several loci).
